Cautiously optimistic, with an upgrade driven by stronger credit supply and demand signaled in the July 2021 SLOOS. The FOMC’s July 28, 2021 statement highlights a strengthening economy, accommodative financial conditions, and continued policy support while noting virus-related risks. The SLOOS corroborates and amplifies the positive tone: banks reported stronger demand for C&I loans from large, middle-market, and small firms, higher borrower inquiries, and easing terms for C&I; they also eased standards for consumer loans (credit cards, autos, other) and reported stronger demand for qualified-mortgage residential loans, with multifamily CRE standards easing as well. Foreign banks similarly reported stronger C&I demand. Reasons for easing included an improved economic outlook, competition, and solid liquidity/capital positions. These broad-based improvements in credit availability and demand suggest a more supportive backdrop for growth than implied by the Financial Stability Report alone, though stability risks (elevated valuations, leverage, and nonbank vulnerabilities) and uneven CRE conditions still temper the outlook. Balancing these, sentiment shifts modestly more positive.
